20.en: "Mankind will evolve, and all those who resist this great transformation will fall behind."

38.en: Humankind is destined to evolve into a psychic species.

46.en: This transformation must be shepherded and defended from those who oppose it.

54.en: Psykers, especially fledgling psykers, must be protected and trained.

76.en: Seek out psykers across the sector to contain or protect them. Train psykers and experiment with psychic powers and phenomena. Be wary of anti-psyker elements across the Imperium, especially those within the Inquisition.

82.en: Polypsykana Inquisitors, many of whom are psykers, believe that Humanity will, and should, eventually ascend to becoming a psychic species. They say the growing number of psykers verifies their beliefs, and the number of Inquisitors following their creed has increased in recent years. They make it their mission to prevent the unnecessary burning of psykers and spend their time monitoring the actions of Inquisitors who might kill rather than capture psykers so they can prevent them from doing so.

86.en: The origins of the Polypsykana are lost to history, as this philosophy may be one of the oldest. Its adherents appear wherever there is a surplus of psykers or tales of psykers of unusual power — and since the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#silence-and-darkness]{Noctis Aeterna}, there has been an excess of psykers in the Macharian Sector.

90.en: There are rumours that a Polypsykana Inquisitor in the Macharian Sector is hunting those who carry the Pariah Gene and executing them on charges of heresy. Other rumours speak of Inquisitors interfering directly with the Black Ships and their damnable cargo. If it proves true, such interference would not be tolerated — and could permanently damage relations between the Inquisition and the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.upGG1JZPDbC7dpJJ]{Adeptus Astra Telepathica}.

94.en: Some Polypsykana experiment with ways of awakening and enhancing psychic abilities to facilitate Mankind’s inevitable evolution. They may study the Warp itself, daemonic lore, xenos, or the anatomy of Humans with and without the Pariah Gene. Their activities are generally conducted secretly, at the far edges of civilisation — with test subjects no one will miss. No Puritan Inquisitor would condone their beliefs, but while the God-Emperor requires psykers, few can dismiss their claims that psykers are, at the least, sometimes useful.

110.en: Polypsykana Inquisitors are utterly fascinated by psykers and hold reverence for their powers and phenomena, so much it might distract them in the moment from whatever task is at hand.

118.en: A psyker Polypsykana Inquisitor may be sympathetic to the plights weighted upon the shoulders of emergent psykers in the Imperium.

126.en: Polypsykana Inquisitors are resolute in their beliefs; when opposed, they cite the Imperium’s reliance on psykers to function, the advances the Imperium has made utilising them, and that, ultimately, the God-Emperor Himself is a psyker.

140.en: One of the Polypsykana Inquisitor’s research stations has been attacked and ransacked by another Inquisitor. The characters must investigate the base to discover who opposes their Patron. Some of the psykers there were taken into custody — track them down before they reveal any more of the Patron’s plans and ideally before they are handed over to the League of Black Ships; rescue or silence them.

148.en: A Black Ship has crashed on the small feudal world of Octavian Secundus. Sabotage is suspected, but the immediate concern is to round up all the psykers who escaped the wreckage. The Polypsykana Inquisitor requests the characters aid in the cleanup but has given them a list of names to investigate — psykers who were aboard — to check if they survived and secretly bring them into custody.
